sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 11.08.2024 at about 00.15 a.m (Midnight) the petitioner had parked his Omini Ambulance on the extreme left side of Bengaluru - Mysore road,
Near Gnanabharathi Junction Metro Station, Bengaluru and standing on the footpath cautiously by observing all the traffic rules to have a cup of tea.

At that time all of a sudden a Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-0269 drove the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life on the extreme left side of the road and lost control over his vehicle and dashed against to the petitioner.
Due to the said impact the petitioner fell down on the road and the rear wheels of the lorry ran over on his both legs.
Immediately after the incident the petitioner was shifted to R.R.Hosptial, wherein he took first aid and thereafter he was shifted to Sai Krupa Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
Due to the accidental injuries he lost income from the date of accident.
He fully disabled to avocation and loss earning capacity.
The accident was caused due to rash and negligence driving of the Lorry, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the vehicle are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2, the respondent No.2 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence it was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-0269.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the petitioner was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL and further the said insured vehicle did not holding valid and effective Permit and FC.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 11.08.2024 at about 1.15 a.m, (Midnight), near Jnanabharathi Junction, Mysore Road, Jnanabharathi Post, Bengaluru City, due to actionable negligence of the driver of lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-0269 ?

2 2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?

6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .P1 to 21 were marked on his behalf.
Dr.S.A.Somashekara was examined as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.22 & 23 documents.
The petitioner also examined the MRO as PW.3, through him got marked Ex.P.24 & 25 documents.

Dr.
Sudhir. B.M, Consultant Plastic surgeon examined as PW.4, through him got marked Ex.P.26 & 27 documents.
The counsel for petitioner filed memo along with extract of DL of petitioner and same is marked with consent of respondent No.1 as Ex.P.28.
The respondent No.1 did not choose to lead any evidence on their behalf.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.1 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.1 crore together.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-0269.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.1 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-0269.

Therefore, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 'In the Affirmative'.
9. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the Lorry.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
10. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :
The petitioner has produced his Aadhar card which is marked as Ex.P.15, as per the above said document wherein his date of birth is reflected as 08.09.1991.
This indicates that he was aged (32 years 11 months 3 days) 33 years on the date of accident.
11. The petitioner deposed that prior to the accident he was working as Ambulance driver and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. and Rs.300/- bata per day.
No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in his evidence affidavit.

It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Manu C M vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164540398/
3 Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023. Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2024.
Therefore, Rs.16,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

12. As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : 1) Crushed injury over the left lower leg (2) Open wound with bone exposed over the left lower leg (3) Left both tibia fibula bone fracture (4) Active bleeding + with pain (5) Deep laceration cut wound over right thigh (6) Right distal femur fracture (7) Right tibia and fibula fracture (8) Right distal femur comminuted fracture.
It is needless to say that the injuries are grievous in nature.
He has produced OPD card of RR Hospital at Ex.P.11, wherein he took treatment on OPD.

13. As per the 3-discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.12 to 14, the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at the below mentioned hospital:

2) Wound debridement and skin grafting with flap for left lower leg (Open Type III B fracture)
continued external fixation till wound heal.

14. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total permanent physical disability of 78% of both lower limbs and 39% disability to the whole body.
It is elicited during the course of cross examination PW.2 categorically admitted that he has not treated the petitioner.
He stated that one fracture was united and two fractures were malunited.
Femur fracture was united, right tibia and left fibula were mal united.
Left tibia was not united.
Non union was because of open fracture.
Mal union was because of multiple fractures.
Tibia and fibula fractures were comminuted fractures.
He admitted that there was no shortening.
15. Further the petitioner also got examined Dr.Sudhir Consultant Plastic Surgeon as PW-4 for assessment of disability.
The PW-4 stated that he was examined the petitioner on 05.07.2025 for assessment of disability.
He assessed disability for both lower limbs.
On clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained disability for the affected bilateral lower limbs at 88% and 29% for the whole body.
During the course of cross examination it is categorically admitted by the PW.4 is that he was not treated the petitioner.
He admitted that he has not know whether previously the petitioner approached Dr.S.A.Somashekara from Victoria Hospital who is orthopedic surgeon.
He stated that he did not know he has assessed disability for range of movements so far as the lower limb as 39%.
He admitted that he has also assessed the disability by applying the combined formula to both lower limb and opined that 29% whole body disability.
He stated that he has also mentioned disability about injury and muscle atropia.
However from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 and PW.4 have assessed the disability on the higher side to the both fractures.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 25%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 25%.
16.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The period of hospitalization of 38 days is proved.

As such during his stay in the Hospital, the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges, as some family member/s of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take his care, by leaving his/her duties.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Accordingly considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day.
is awarded under this head.
17. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.

Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under this Manu C M vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164540398/

18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 6 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.99,000/- (16,500 X 6) under this head.
19. MEDICAL EXPENSES :
As per the bills marked at Ex.P16, the petitioner has spent Rs.10,97,223/- towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.10,97,223/- which is rounded off to Rs.10,97,200/- towards medical expenses.
20. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '16'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.7,92,000/- (Rs.16,500 X 12 X 16 X 25/100) is awarded under this head.
21. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of is life.
Hence a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded under this head.
22. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES :

The Orthopedic doctor(PW.2) stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants,
control of infection and achieving union which would cost around Rs.1,00,000/- in private set up and the plastic surgeon (PW.4) stated that the petitioner (1) Firstly require surgery for non-healing ulcer with exposed bone for which free latissimus dorsi muscle flap / free ALT flap to be done costing approximately Rs.5,00,000/-
(2) Secondly undergo removal of implants - Bilateral leg and right thigh, the cost of surgery will be approximately Rs.2,00,000/-
(3) Later, he will require surgery for nerve surgery with foot drop - Tendon transfer / Free functional muscle transfer, the surgery will cost approximately Rs.4,00,000/-.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants and nerve surgery with foot drop etc., for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.3,00,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
25. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the Lorry thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
26. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.24,63,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (Excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 70% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 30% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
